Title: GB-Glasgow: JFC6C/00031 Exercise Prescription Licences
Description:
Exercise prescription is a core element of rehabilitation of injuries in Defence.  Exercise description, frequency and progression must be clearly documented by the clinician in order to provide a comprehensive medical record and to act as a reference document for the patient to ensure the delivery of a safe and effective individual exercise programme. A hosted software solution is required which enables the production and digital sharing of bespoke individual exercise programmes. 
      
      The Contractor is to provide a hosted software solution which:
      •	Allows the production of bespoke, individual exercise programmes .
      •	Has a broad ranging catalogue of exercises relevant to the physical rehabilitation of musculoskeletal injury, neurological injury and disease.
      •	Produces exercise sheets with clear pictorial reference which has an editable written description (allowing modification of elements such as resistance, frequency and number of repetitions).
      •	Produces templates, which can be shared with other users, for common individual exercise programmes .
      •	Is capable of supporting a variety of media.
      •	Produces exercise prescriptions which can be published and shared with the patient via digital transmission and produce a record which can be stored in the e-health record (eHR). Once published the record must be non-modifiable.
      •	Has a unique login for each authorised clinician. 
      
      
      A web based portal is required, which is accessible from any worldwide web terminal. The exercise prescription output must comply with the Healthcare Professions Council (HCPC) standard for medical documentation (physiotherapy standards). In addition the portal must allow the development of additional Authority exercise programmes for specialist areas such as catered for at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre and the Royal Centre for Defence Medicine.
      
      The evaluation criterion for this requirement is Most Economically Advantageous to Tender (MEAT) with an agreed scoring weighting of 60 Technical and 40 Price. 
      
      Should you have any questions please contact Aileen McLynn, Commercial Manager on DefComrclCC-JFC6a@mod.uk.

Title: Repair of a Quantity not to exceed 100 of the X200 Transmissions for the Bulldog Armoured Fighting Vehicle Platform
Description:
Babcock acting as the Authority's Agent, intend to negotiate a single source enabling contract with Caterpillar Shrewsbury Ltd, for the repair of a quantity to not exceed 100 of the X200 Transmissions fitted to the Bulldog Armoured Fighting Vehicle Platform. 

It is considered that this Contract can be placed using the Negotiated procedure without prior publication pursuant to Article 28(1)(e) of the Directive 2009/81/EC(Regulation 16(1)(a)(ii) of the UK Defence and Security Public Contract Regulations 2011) for technical reasons. 

Allison Transmissions are the OEM, all drawings and specifications of the X200 were developed with internal funding and are proprietary to them, and are a highly specialised type of transmission modified to fit the specific application. This requirement is for the repair and reconditioning of the X200. Without the detailed technical information referenced above a Supplier would not be able to ensure repaired and reconditioned X200's were fit for purpose in accordance with the original design specifications, or maintain configuration control such as build standards, drawing and test specifications. The X200 is part of the safety critical part of the Bulldog powertrain and is therefore essential to the safe operation of the Bulldog platforms and maintaining the status of the safety case at ALARP. 

Caterpillar Shrewsbury Ltd are the only agent in the UK that Allison licence to carry out work on their range of defence products and as a consequence Caterpillar Shrewsbury Ltd is the only supplier with access to the design information and technical details, data and knowledge necessary to fulfil the requirement. The design information and technical details, data and knowledge are not available to any other supplier. 

This notice is not a request for expressions of interest so please do not apply to be invited to tender. This notice advises that the UK Ministry of Defence is to place a single source non-qualifying contract with the named supplier to satisfy repairs to critical assets whilst an enduring solution is progressed.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, DIO, Defence Infrastructure Organisation (DIO)
Title: Oil Fuel Depot Gosport, Tank Farm Project
Description:
The Oil Fuel Depot (OFD) Gosport has been operational for more than 100 years and some of the current operational infrastructure was constructed before World War One. All tanks are of rivited plate steel construction. This type of tank construction ceased in the commercial sector in the 1960's.The existing tanks have undergone packages of maintenance works to extend their out of service dates as agreed with the competent authority, the Health and Safety Executive. 
      The requirement is to raze and rebuild the tanks and associated infrastructure at the Oil Fuel Depot in Gosport whilst keeping the site open and maintaining operational capability for the customer. To achieve this requirement the works will need to be completed in a phased delivery approach, bringing new tanks online to align with the existing tank "out of service" dates in order to maintain the fuel holding requirements. 
      The Contractor will be responsible for all activities associated with the raze and rebuild element, including but not limited to demolition and targeted remediation activities on the new Tank Farm footprint. The new tank farm scope will include but is not limited to:
      •	Fuel Storage Tanks - Envisaged 6 primary storage tanks with 5 smaller supporting tanks.
      •	Bunding in accordance with current operational standards.
      •	Associated pipework
      •	Fuel delivery systems including pump sets
      •	Admin / control room
      •	Security elements in line with MOD Standards.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, DSTL, Defence Science & Technology Laboratory (DSTL)
Title: R-Cloud Framework Renewal
Description:
The Defence Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl), which is part of the UK Ministry of Defence, wishes to renew it's commercial framework for Science and Technology (S&T) research contracts, known as R-Cloud (Research Cloud). Dstl places extensive fundamental, experimental and applied research with industry and academic suppliers and wants to broaden access for this supply base, reducing the cost of trading with Dstl and enabling agile contracting. R-Cloud complements Dstl's other contracting mechanisms and academic and industry suppliers of S&T research will be invited to pre-qualify onto it to join Dstl's research supplier community. The ownership of any intellectual property generated will remain with the suppliers. Although this requirement is exempt from the Procurement Regulations as it is for Research activities, Dstl is advertising and competing for new participants. For existing R-Cloud suppliers further information and guidance about this renewal process will be published on the R-Cloud portal https://rcloud.dstl.gov.uk/ . New suppliers interested in registering for R-Cloud should apply by  e-mail to dstlrcloud@dstl.gov.uk , giving their name, address and contact details and will then be contacted to be included in the renewal process.
      
      This call relates to a series of R-Cloud frameworks covering eight Capability Areas as follows: 
      •	Command, Control, Communication & Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR)
      •	Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN)
      •	Counter Terrorism and Security (CT&S)
      •	Cyber
      •	Human Capability (HC)    
      •	Integrated Survivability (IS)
      •	Platform Systems (PS)
      •	Weapons
      
      R-Cloud provides a low barrier to entry for potential suppliers and offers direct access to Dstl's current and future research requirements. Academic and industrial suppliers of research are invited to pre-qualify onto the R-Cloud framework. A standard form of contract has been drawn up which details the terms and conditions for entry onto the R-Cloud framework. Acceptance of these terms and conditions is mandatory.

Title: WO0268 Ludgershall Perham Primary School
Description:
Following an Army Basing Review undertaken by the Ministry of Defence (MOD) in March 2003, it has been decided by the MOD that the Brigade Headquarters of the British Army Reaction Force is to be relocated to the Salisbury Plain Training Area with three Armoured Infantry Brigades. 

As a consequence, an additional 4,000 military personnel and their families will be relocated to Tidworth, Ludgershall, Bulford and Larkhill. This process has already started and is due to be completed in circa 2019.

A major implication of this Army re-basing programme is that additional facilities such as Schools, Housing, Leisure Facilities, Health and Social Services need to be provided to meet the increase in population in the affected areas.

Within the Ludgershall area, it has been identified that there is a need for the development of a new two form entry primary school including a thirty-place nursery to be located on a circa 2.3-hectare parcel of land provided by the MOD via a Section 106 Agreement within the site of the former Corruna Barracks in Ludgershall. The requirement is that the new school and nursery is operationally ready to accept pupils by September 2019 which is the purpose of this tender opportunity.

The Workshop Tools & Equipment (WTE) team are part of the Support & Test Equipment (STE) area in Operational Infrastructure (OI) and are responsible for the through life management of workshop tools and equipment. WTE/Workshop manages a wide range of metal, wood working and garage machinery at more than 180 locations in the UK and overseas. In order to maintain the serviceability of the legacy equipment, its operational output and most importantly, the safety of the operators, this contract for the supply, servicing, repair and commissioning/de-commissioning of metal, wood working and garage equipment was placed.

Only one technically compliant response to the PQQ was received following Contract Notice. It would therefore not be possible to demonstrate Value For Money under the initial procedure. EXPERIMENTATION DATA CAPTURE OVERVIEW OF USER FOR ARMY WARFIGHTING EXPERIMENT 2018
      The Army Warfighting Experiment 2018 (AWE18), Autonomous Warrior (Land) (AW(L) is the Army's premier experimentation activity for 2018, taking place in and around Salisbury Plain between 12 November 2018 and 12 December 2018. 
      A stand-alone system, deployed to personnel through portable handheld devices, is required to assist in the planning, designing, conducting, collecting and reporting of information gathered during AWE18. The requirements of the system are:
      -	the ability to have specific experiment design/data loaded prior to the experiment commencement date.
      -	to capture and collate real time multimedia data from a variety of sources such as photo, video and text. 
      -	to collect time and location specific information against pre-set criteria, for a variety of different equipment. 
      -	to take information gathered to produce reports in a variety of standard text formats on equipment performance. 
      -	to be able to produce evidence (based on inputs) to enable the evaluation of performance against pre-set criteria of individual and groups of equipment during the experiment. 
      -	to withstand potential adverse weather conditions. 
      -	to permit data collected during experimentation to be shared between users and extracted and stored by the user.
      -	to be a secure system for the users access only for the duration of the contract
      -	no experimentation data collected by the user will be held by the contractor at the end of the experimental period.
      -	50 portable hand held devices will be required from between 1st November 2018 and 31st December 2018.  
      -	provision of train-the-trainer for 5 'super-users' for the systems will be required prior to the experiment commencement date.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, ISTAR, Situational Awareness Command and Control (SACC) Delivery Team
Title: Provision of Technical Support to the UK Link 16 Frequency Clearance Agreement
Description:
The Situational Awareness Command and Control Deliver Team, (SACC DT), part of the UK Ministry of Defence (MoD), intends to award a new Contract for the support, repair, maintenance and storage of the Frequency Clearance (FC) System. This Contract will be for an initial period of 24 (24) months with two (2) twelve (12) month extension options.   
      The principal requirements of the Link 16 Frequency Clearance Support contract are as follows:
      •	To undertake compatibility testing of Link 16 with Communications Navigation and Surveillance (CNS) systems operating in the 960-1215MHz frequency band, using the government furnished FC Test equipment, known as the 8 Net Signal Source. This is a collection of bespoke test equipment enabling interference testing of Link 16 on civilian aeronautical CNS equipment, as required by the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) under the terms of the FC Agreement (FCA). 
      •	To support of all aspects of Link 16 network management, monitoring, design, planning and the technical aspects of the FCA to support the Joint Data Link Management Organisation (JDLMO), including working with the JDLMO to maintain compliance with the terms of the FCA, including the CAA audit process, and maintaining clearance to radiate for all Link 16 platforms in the UK Flight Information Region. 
      •	To manage and maintain the Link 16 FCA Safety Management System (FCA SMS) and all associated documentation on behalf of the MoD and CAA. The FCA SMS includes the Safety and Environmental Management Plan, Baseline Safety Case, Terminal Safety Cases (Generic and Specific variants) and Platform Safety Cases. A Subject Matter Expert is required to manage the FCA SMS including technically reviewing Terminal and Platform Safety Cases and staffing them though the FCA Safety Committee approvals process. A detailed knowledge of the background and content of the above documents is required to deliver this requirement.  
      •	In order to deliver this requirement a detailed knowledge of how Link 16 interferes with CNS systems, and the ability to undertake interference assessments against the following equipment is required: Distance Measuring Equipment (DME), Tactical Air Navigation Aids (TACAN), Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR), Automatic Dependent Surveillance (Broadcast) ADS-B, 1090 MHz Multilateration, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and L-Band Digital Aeronautical Communications (L-DAC
